column1: # THE OTHER OFFICES — FIFTY-ONE DEATH-INDEX VOLUMES, FOUR NAMES OUT, AND AN INSTRUMENT THAT NOW PROVES ITS OWN EYESIGHT.
# Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA. Kreuzberg P Rep. 510 · Reinickendorf P Rep. 130 · Spandau I P Rep. 480 · Neukölln P Rep. 380.
# Read 7 October 2026. Work list rows 252 and 253.
# WHY THESE FOUR OFFICES AND NOT SCHÖNEBERG. Schöneberg's sixty-one volumes were closed on 21 September.
# These are the offices the people themselves lived in: AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER at Mehringdamm 109,
# which is KREUZBERG · FRIEDRICH LEIPHOLZ at Schwabstraße 4, which is REINICKENDORF · CHARLOTTE LEIBHOLZ
# of the Hasenheide, which is NEUKÖLLN · ERNA of Streitstraße and HILDE of Wiesbadener Straße, SPANDAU.
field
column2: value

column1: # ---------------- WHAT CAME OUT: FOUR PEOPLE OF THE NAME ----------------
*** FRITZ LEIPHOLZ — STERBEREGISTER SPANDAU 1985 NR. 2926 ***
column2: Died 24 NOVEMBER 1985. "ev." and "verw." — Protestant and WIDOWED. P Rep. 480 Nr. 2356, page 92, between Leifke verh. Steiner and Lemcke verh. Gerhardt. THE PAGE IS TYPEWRITTEN, not script, so the reading is not an interpretation; it was confirmed at the image at full resolution and the crop is in the scratch notes. A death entry of that vintage carries the address, the birth date or age, the birthplace and the informant, and it is orderable by number.

column1: is Fritz the Friedrich of Schwabstraße 4
column2: A CANDIDATE AND NOT AN IDENTIFICATION, AND THE REASON FOR SAYING SO IS THAT THE STORY FITS TOO WELL. Work list row 251 tracks FRIEDRICH LEIPHOLZ, Angestellter at Tegel 1957-59 and PENSIONÄR at Schwabstraße 4, REINICKENDORF, from 1961, in the telephone books to 1973-74 and GONE FROM 1974-75. Reinickendorf's own death registers 1974 to 1981 were read in full on 21 September and he is in none of them, so row 251 concluded he moved and died elsewhere. FRITZ IS THE ORDINARY SHORT FORM OF FRIEDRICH and Spandau is the next borough west. THAT IS A SHAPE, NOT A DOCUMENT. Nothing here gives a birth date, an address or a wife's name, and this archive has got a man wrong on a name and a trade before. THE CERTIFICATE WOULD SETTLE IT.

column1: *** MARIE LEIPHOLZ — STERBEREGISTER REINICKENDORF 1988 NR. 2306 ***
column2: Died 5 NOVEMBER 1988, "ev.". P Rep. 130 Nr. 1484, page 76, between Leinkram and Leisegang. Also typewritten and also confirmed at the image. SHE IS NOT FRITZ'S WIDOW AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE WHOLE POINT: Fritz is entered VERWITWET in November 1985, so his wife was already dead; Marie died three years after him. The tidy reading is the wrong one and it is recorded here so that nobody reaches for it again.

column1: and a neighbour on Marie's own page
column2: NR. 189 of 1988, four lines above her, is LEINKRAM, Gertrud Auguste Rudolfine, "mosaisch" — a Jewish death in Reinickendorf in 1988. Nothing to do with this family. Noted because the confession column in these volumes is real information and is easy to stop reading.

column1: *** GERTRUD ELLA MEIRITZ née LEIPHOLZ — STERBEREGISTER SPANDAU 1993 NR. 2047 ***
column2: Died 29 AUGUST 1993. P Rep. 480 Nr. 2842, entered TWICE as the series always enters a married woman — "Leipholz, Gertrud Ella" on page 72 under L and "Meiritz, geb. Leipholz, Gertrud Ella" on page 80 under M. A LEIPHOLZ-BORN WOMAN WHO MARRIED OUT, which is exactly the case row 253 warned the L block has to be read for.

column1: how her register number was established, since the image could not be read
column2: THE 1993 SCAN IS A DOUBLE EXPOSURE — two leaves superimposed — and nothing on it is legible. The text layer is a clean transcription but it prints the NAMES as one block and the REGISTER NUMBERS as another, with nothing joining them. SO THE PAIRING WAS TESTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Across the whole volume, 2,396 distinct (forenames, death-date) keys were built and paired positionally: 2,394 carry EXACTLY ONE register number and only two carry more, both of which are plainly two different people (two Ernas dying on 15 May; and 550/551, consecutive). AND HER OWN ENTRY IS ITS OWN CONTROL — row 27 under L on page 72 and row 9 under M on page 80, two unrelated positions in two blocks on two pages, BOTH RETURN 2047/1993. Published on that basis and the basis is stated.

column1: *** LEOKADIA LOWINSKI née BARANIAK — STERBEREGISTER NEUKÖLLN NR. 815 ***
column2: Died 19 March, in the volume covering 1978 AND 1979, so THE YEAR IS NOT YET FIXED. "kath." P Rep. 380 Nr. 716, entered twice — "Baraniak verh. Lowinski" on page 6 and "Lowinski geb. Baraniak" on page 92. *** ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT THIS FAMILY, AND VALUABLE FOR THAT. *** Leokadia, Baraniak and katholisch all point at the POLISH CATHOLIC LOWINSKI strand — the one the family tree already confused with Derrick's line when it made Manfred and Joachim sons of Alfred of Przasnysz, a Polish Catholic farm labourer. What it buys is the spelling LOWINSKI alive in post-war Berlin and attached to somebody else. NOT CONFIRMED AT THE IMAGE; the reading is the OCR's and the year is open.

column1: # ---------------- THE INSTRUMENT, AND THE GUARD IT DID NOT HAVE THIS MORNING ----------------
*** EVERY VOLUME NOW SCORES ITS OWN TEXT LAYER BEFORE ITS SILENCE COUNTS ***
column2: Row 253 measured the fault by hand and this sweep would have walked straight into it. KREUZBERG 1983 is labelled "Durchsuchbares PDF durch OCR-Texterkennung" and across 211 pages its layer yields SCHMIDT 6, MÜLLER 4, BECKER 0 — because the register is HANDWRITTEN and the OCR caught the printed headings and almost nothing else. The first pass of this sweep returned twelve clean Kreuzberg brackets built on exactly that layer. THE SCANNER NOW COUNTS SIX COMMON SURNAMES IN EVERY VOLUME and refuses to call anything a negative below 0.15 of them a page.

column1: and the numbers separate the two classes without argument
column2: KREUZBERG 1983 SCORES 0.095 A PAGE. KREUZBERG 1984 SCORES 1.272 — THIRTEEN TIMES MORE, and the file drops from 125 MB to 33 MB in the same step, because the series changes from photographed handwriting to a typed index. Across all fifty-one volumes the legible ones run 0.93 to 1.96 and the blind ones 0.00 to 0.095. There is no middle.

column1: *** AND READING EVERY PAGE REPLACED THE BAND, WHICH IS WHAT MADE THE SEPTEMBER FALSE NEGATIVES POSSIBLE ***
column2: The 21 September method read the middle third of a volume and Kreuzberg 1980 and 1981 came back "no hit" with their last Le- word at Leipelt and Leimbach, both of which sort BEFORE Leipholz. This sweep reads EVERY PAGE OF EVERY VOLUME, which dissolves that fault and the two-alphabets-in-one-book fault with it. The two-sided bracket is kept as a redundant check rather than as the proof of coverage.

column1: *** AND THE BRACKET TURNS OUT NOT TO BE A PROOF OF COVERAGE AT ALL IN SOME OF THESE BOOKS ***
column2: NEUKÖLLN 1967-1968 RUNS BY MONTH AND DATE INSIDE EACH LETTER, NOT ALPHABETICALLY — page 263 opens L with Lienau, Lorenz, Liebster, Lorenz, Liesegang, Liedtke, Lawischka, Lohse. A "nearest name before and after" test means nothing against an order like that, and any method that narrows to a sub-range of the letter would miss the name outright. ONLY READING EVERY PAGE OF THE LETTER WORKS. Schöneberg's volumes from 1954 group by month the same way, which is why that run read every page of its L block too.

column1: the controls the sweep was proved on before it was trusted
column2: TWO, BOTH REPRODUCED. SCHÖNEBERG 1975, the known positive: it returned "Leipholz | Erna Frida Else | 13.1. | 79 | ev" on page 54, which is the entry this archive already holds. KREUZBERG 1982, the known negative with two alphabetical sequences: nothing, bracketed Leinrich to Leitz, matching what was recorded in September.

column1: a technical note, because it cost an hour
column2: pypdf will NOT read these over HTTP range requests. Asked for one page of a 4 MB volume it pulled all 4,404 KB in 68 requests and took 146 seconds — range requests buy nothing when the library wants every byte. The September run used pdf.js, which fetches only the content streams. This run fetched each volume once, read it, and deleted it.

column1: # ---------------- THE NEGATIVES, OFFICE BY OFFICE ----------------
KREUZBERG 1984 TO 1994 — ELEVEN YEARS, NO LEIBHOLZ AND NO LEIPHOLZ
column2: P Rep. 510 Nr. 762, 781, 800, 819, 838, 920, 1066, 1184, 1284, 1456, 1471. Every volume read page by page, every one bracketed on both sides, every one scoring 1.13 to 1.58 control names a page. The gap, year by year: 1984 Lehmann·Leidig — 1985 Lehnart·Leidreiter — 1986 Lehnert·Leichner — 1987 Lehrfeld·Leidig — 1988 Lehmann·Leike — 1989 Lehr·Leider — 1990 Lehninger·Leissring — 1991 Lehrke·Leidhold — 1992 Lehwald·Leifert — 1993 Lehnicke·Leisring — 1994 Leibfried·Lemke.

column1: KREUZBERG 1983 — WITHDRAWN AS A TEXT NEGATIVE, AND IT DOES NOT MATTER
column2: P Rep. 510 Nr. 743 scores 0.095 and is BLIND. Its bracket is not evidence of anything and is not published as one. IT WAS ALREADY READ AT THE IMAGE ON 22 SEPTEMBER — L/1983 is pages 96 to 105, bounded by the tail of K and the opening of M, twelve months in order, no Leibholz, no Leipholz, no Kerger — so the year is covered by the other route and nothing is lost.

column1: *** AND THAT CLOSES WORK LIST ROW 253 AND CANCELS THE WORK IT WAS HOLDING ***
column2: Row 253 planned to read ELEVEN MORE VOLUMES AT THE IMAGE — "about ten L pages each, two legible half-screenshots per page, roughly 220 reads" — on the premise that Kreuzberg stayed handwritten to 1994. IT DOES NOT. The series changes at 1984 and the text layer from there is as good as Schöneberg's. AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER DID NOT DIE IN KREUZBERG BETWEEN 1980 AND 1994. She left the telephone book at Mehringdamm 109 after 1979-80, she was ninety-one, and the borough has now been asked the whole question. A move into a home in another borough remains at least as likely as a death, and that is where the row goes next.

column1: REINICKENDORF 1982 TO 1994 — THIRTEEN YEARS, ONE HIT
column2: P Rep. 130 Nr. 1478-1490. All thirteen legible (0.93 to 1.75 a page), all bracketed. The only name of the family's letters in the whole run is MARIE LEIPHOLZ in 1988. FRIEDRICH LEIPHOLZ IS IN NONE OF THEM — which, set beside the 1974-1981 run read on 21 September, means REINICKENDORF IS NOW READ WITHOUT A GAP FROM 1974 TO 1994 AND HE IS NOT IN IT. Twenty-one consecutive years. He left Schwabstraße 4 during 1974 and he did not die in that borough afterwards.

column1: SPANDAU I 1983 TO 1994 — TWELVE YEARS, TWO HITS
column2: P Rep. 480 Nr. 1248, 2332, 2356, 2459, 2522, 2604, 2605, 2709, 2710, 2841, 2842, 2879. All twelve legible (1.26 to 1.96 a page), all bracketed. FRITZ LEIPHOLZ 1985 and GERTRUD ELLA MEIRITZ née LEIPHOLZ 1993, both above. No Leibholz in any year. Set beside Spandau 1982, read on 21 September, which gave the Leibholz-born woman who married SCHÖNFELD (Nr. 1486, "mos.", work list row 254), SPANDAU HAS NOW PRODUCED THREE PEOPLE OF THESE TWO SPELLINGS AND IS THE RICHEST OF THE FOUR OFFICES.

column1: SPANDAU I 1982-1986, P Rep. 480 Nr. 2458 — INCONCLUSIVE AND SAID SO
column2: 202 pages, control score 0.03, BLIND. It overlaps years that the single-year volumes cover, but whether it indexes the SAME deaths or a separate register is not established, so its silence is recorded as unread rather than as a negative. It is the one volume of the fifty-one that is neither read nor closed.

column1: NEUKÖLLN 1969 TO 1992 — TEN VOLUMES BY TEXT, NO LEIBHOLZ AND NO LEIPHOLZ
column2: P Rep. 380 Nr. 711-717, 754, 904, 956. All ten legible (1.14 to 1.83 a page) and bracketed. What the run DOES hold, recorded so a later reader does not rediscover them: LEIBNITZ geb. Teske 1970/71 Nr. 1462 (twinned under T) · LEIPNER 1972/73 Nr. 1785 · LEIPNITZ 1974/75 · LEIBNER 1974/75 Nr. 976 · LEIPNER 1978/79 Nr. 3388 and Nr. 1428 · LEIPNITZ 1982/84 Nr. 1221 · LEIBNITZ 1988/90 Nr. 2156 · LEIPNER and LEIBNER 1991/92. NOT ONE OF THEM IS A LEIBHOLZ OR A LEIPHOLZ.

column1: *** NEUKÖLLN 1967-1968 — NO TEXT LAYER AT ALL, SO IT WAS READ AT THE IMAGE ***
column2: P Rep. 380 Nr. 710, 570 pages, 334 MB, and ZERO pages carrying text. THE L BLOCK IS PAGES 263 TO 289, bounded by the end of K on 262 and the opening of M on 290, and every page of it was read. NO LEIBHOLZ AND NO LEIPHOLZ. Near misses in it: LEIBKÜCHLER geb. Hennig · LEIPNER geb. Moye · LEIPNER, Richard Ernst · LEIPERT, Richard Hermann · LEISSNER, Hermann Wilhelm · LEIB geb. Schwenk.

column1: and this volume is why the bracket cannot be the proof of coverage
column2: IT IS NOT ALPHABETICAL INSIDE THE LETTER. Page 263 opens L under "Januar 1967" with Lienau, Lorenz, Liebster, Lorenz, Liesegang, Liedtke, Lawischka, Lohse — the entries run BY MONTH AND DATE. A nearest-name-either-side test is meaningless against that order, and any method that narrows to part of the letter would walk past the name. Only reading every page of the letter works, which is what was done.

column1: *** NEUKÖLLN 1985-1987 — NO TEXT LAYER, SCANNED MIRRORED, AND THE PAGES ARE OUT OF ORDER ***
column2: P Rep. 380 Nr. 822, 509 pages, zero with text, and EVERY PAGE IS A MIRROR IMAGE — the film was scanned reversed, and it is read by flipping it. It holds THREE SEPARATE ALPHABETS, one per year, and ALL THREE L BLOCKS WERE FOUND AND READ. (1) Pages 80-88: the chain runs LEIBLICH verh. Herbst then LEICHMANN geb. Langier, with nothing between, and LEIHE then LEIPNER geb. Bolinski. (2) Pages 251-258: page 253 runs Lehrmann · LEIDGEBEL verh. Diehereit · LEISS verh. Mackrahen · Lemcke, straight through both slots. (3) Page 421: LEHNUCK verh. Bosse then LEIDING verh. Ocker, and LEIPELT verh. Rudnick then LEMKE geb. Dietz. *** NO LEIBHOLZ AND NO LEIPHOLZ IN ANY OF THE THREE. ***

column1: and the page order in that volume is genuinely shuffled, which had to be proved rather than assumed
column2: The 251-258 block reads in the order 252, 251, 254, 253, 256, 255, 258, 257 — and the SURNAMES CHAIN UNBROKEN ACROSS ALL EIGHT, Labrenz to Luxens, each page's last name sorting immediately before the next page's first. That continuity is what makes the block a complete reading rather than eight disconnected pages.

column1: *** SO NEUKÖLLN IS NOW CLOSED, 1967 TO 1992, TWELVE VOLUMES, NOT ONE OF THE NAME ***
column2: CHARLOTTE LEIBHOLZ OF THE HASENHEIDE, who is in the Berlin directory from 1957 to 1967, DID NOT DIE IN NEUKÖLLN IN THE TWENTY-SIX YEARS AFTER SHE LAST APPEARS IN IT. The same caution as always applies and this archive's own control case is the reason for it: Heinrich Leibholz vanished from the directory after 1942 and did not die until 1948. She may have moved, entered a home in another borough, married, or died in a hospital registering to a different office.
